title: Your immeasurables
hookLine: a full sitting that moves through all four

cards: Nothing new to learn today. Two weeks ago, you walked into a house with four rooms. Since then you've learned each room's name, what it looks like, and its lookalike, the near enemy that tries to move in.
You've sent kindness in every direction, like the trumpeter heard on all four sides, and matched the room to the person.
Today you walk through the whole house, one room after another, and see what it's like to have all four.

teach.b: Here's the fortnight in one breath. Brahmavihara: four sublime dwellings. Metta, kindness: its near enemy is clinging, its far enemy ill will, which softens with practice.
Karuna, compassion, the heart that trembles at another's pain; its lookalike is pity, and the fix is beside, not above. Compassion even for the one who harms, because they are heading for pain.
Mudita, gladness: their joy is joy, and envy softens into it. Upekkha, equanimity: balanced, not cold, and never the shrug of indifference.
Then three ways to hold them all. Like a trumpeter: boundless, in every direction. The right room: each quality for the moment that calls for it.
Living there: a home, not a visit. The texts list them in this order, and teachers give a reason. Kindness is the ground.
Compassion is kindness meeting pain. Gladness is kindness meeting joy.
Equanimity comes last. As some teachers put it, equanimity without the other three can go cold, and the other three without equanimity can burn you out. Together, the texts say, they have no measure.
A full sitting can move through all four, a few minutes each, starting close, with yourself or someone easy, and widening until no one is left out.
Today, a short version; a longer one is waiting for any quiet evening.

how: A traditional brahmavihara sitting moves through kindness, compassion, gladness and equanimity in turn, often beginning with oneself or a benefactor and widening to a neutral person, a difficult person and finally all beings.

o: a count of how much kindness you've given away
four separate feelings, each kept for its own day
all four qualities practiced together, with no edge

games.q: match each immeasurable to its lookalike or its line.

s: equanimity comes first in the list
it comes last, so it rests on warmth and doesn't go cold.
the immeasurables are meant to widen until no one is left out
they start close and grow until they have no measure.
the other three without equanimity can burn you out
that's one reason teachers keep all four together.

games.q: you're starting a full four-room sitting. where does the traditional order begin?
o: with the hardest person you know.
with yourself or someone easy to love, then widening.
with all beings everywhere at once.
games.why: the Visuddhimagga starts with oneself, then someone dear, someone neutral and someone difficult, widening until no one is left out.

practice: Four rooms, about thirty seconds each: kindness, wishing someone easy to love well and letting it widen; compassion, leaning toward someone hurting; gladness, being glad with someone who's doing well.
Last, equanimity: hold them all, and yourself, with a steady heart that cares and lets go. The longer sitting gives each room three minutes, twelve in all.

wordCard.voice: Your immeasurables. Kindness, compassion, gladness and equanimity, practiced together until they have no edge.

orig.note: Pali appamaññā: the immeasurables, the four qualities with no edge.

carryVoice: Your line: immeasurable. Tomorrow a new part of the path begins: the Buddha's great teaching on mindfulness. Two hundred forty-five days, and counting.
